label: Quarters kept per row
tooltip: How many past cells each row keeps. TradingView allows 500 boxes in total, so (rows x this value) + projected cells must stay under 500. The QT cycle boxes (QT CYCLES SETTINGS) share the same 500-box limit, so lower this or the QT history days if cells disappear.

label: Show Sequence Label (e.g. 3-3-3)
tooltip: Shows the current sequence of the lowest visible cycle.

label: Label Position
tooltip: Top / Bottom = label at the right edge of the pane. Corner = small box in the top-left corner.

disabled: Chưa được port đầy đủ trong QT+ JS; giữ nguyên, xem README indicator.

label: Minimum Chain Length
tooltip: Only highlight when at least this many adjacent visible timeframes are aligned.

label: Highlight Chains
tooltip: ON: cells in a chain also get the strong colour and the style below is applied.

label: Highlight Style
tooltip:
Cell colour only = chain cells keep their strong quarter colour and all other cells fade (no extra marking).
Background color = pane background while any chain is active.
Boxes = thick chain-coloured border on every cell in a chain.
Separate ribbon row = an extra bottom row showing the chain length.

label: Transparency for non-preferred (faded) cells
tooltip: Applies to every cell whose sequence is not preferred.

label: Show Quarter Backgrounds
tooltip: OFF: normal quarter cells have no fill (preferred/chain highlights still show).

label: Show Vertical Lines at quarter starts
Show only pure sequences (111 / 222 / 333 / 444)
tooltip: ON: only pure sequences can be preferred (colours, table, alerts, projection).

label: Allow Q4-Q1 bridge
tooltip: ON: Q4 next to Q1 (either direction) continues a chain.

label: Nano row shows sequence text
tooltip: ON: cells show the sequence (e.g. 3-2-3, tiny text). OFF: cells show Q#.

label: Show row labels
tooltip: Row names anchored at the leftmost visible bar. TradingView redraws chart-anchored labels on scroll, which can cause a brief flicker.

label: Row label text size
disabled: Chưa được port đầy đủ trong QT+ JS; giữ nguyên, xem README indicator.

label: Timezone
tooltip: Default America/New_York. The trading day starts at 18:00 in the selected timezone.

label: Nano sequences
tooltip: Comma separated list, e.g. 2-2-2,3-3-3. Nano sequence = 90m-Micro-Nano.

label: Micro sequences
tooltip: Micro sequence = Daily-90m-Micro.

label: 90min sequences
tooltip: 90m sequence = Weekly-Daily-90m.

label: Daily sequences
tooltip: Daily sequence = Monthly-Weekly-Daily.

label: Weekly sequences
tooltip: Weekly sequence = Yearly-Monthly-Weekly.

label: Monthly sequences
tooltip: Monthly sequence = Quadrenial-Yearly-Monthly.

label: Yearly sequences
tooltip: Yearly sequence = Quadrenial-Yearly-Yearly.

label: Filter high probability sequences
tooltip:
ON: the list below REPLACES the per-cycle lists above for every cycle (exact matches only). OFF: the per-cycle lists are used.
Listed sequences get the strong quarter colour; all others fade.

label: High probability sequences
tooltip: Write the sequences you want, separated by commas. Used when the filter above is ON.

label: Include the next sequence
tooltip: Per-cycle lists only: a listed 3-3-3 also matches the following 3-3-4 (last digit + 1, up to Q4).

label: Colour only preferred sequences
tooltip: ON: cells are filled ONLY while their sequence is preferred (special colours). Other cells stay empty (border only).

label: Mark 369 sequences
tooltip: Marks sequences whose digit sum reduces (digital root) to 3, 6 or 9 with a thick border.

label: Treat 369 sequences as preferred
tooltip: ON: 369 sequences also count as preferred (colours, table, alerts, projection).

label: Friday as Q4
tooltip:
OFF: Mon=Q1, Tue=Q2, Wed=Q3, Thu=Q4, Fri=Q0.
ON: Friday is also counted as Q4.

label: Project rest of session
tooltip: Draws every row forward to the next 18:00 session roll (clock-pure, so upcoming quarters, sequences and chains are known in advance). Projected cells have dotted borders. Redrawn once per bar.

label: Max projected cells per row
tooltip: Caps projected cells per row to protect the 500-box limit.
